_comment: Per-user brand config. Copy this file to brand.json (gitignored) and fill in your values. The shape supports a parent org with N child brands — useful if you have multiple products posted under one company. If you only have one brand, just leave a single key under `brands`.
_resolution: Skills resolve which brand to target like this: (1) use the slug passed as the first arg if given (e.g. `/x-warm myproject`); (2) else use `default_brand`. Then they pull values from `brands.<slug>.<platform>.<key>`. Org-level values (LinkedIn company id, parent name) are shared across all brands.
_essential_tabs_comment: URLs that scripts/launch_browser.sh ensures are open after Chrome boots. Combined with Chrome's --restore-last-session flag (set automatically by the launch script), this means: clean restart → Chrome restores prior tabs (no-op for verifier); crash → flag forces restore (no 'Restore?' prompt to click); fresh profile / closed-by-mistake tabs → verifier adds the missing ones. Pin them in Chrome (right-click tab → Pin) for visual + accident-resistance. Note: matcher is HOST-level — if you list two URLs on the same domain (e.g. two X handles), the verifier opens only the first one when no x.com tabs exist at all; --restore-last-session handles the multi-tab case correctly when the previous session is intact.

org._comment: Org-level info shared across all brands. LinkedIn company-page posts go FROM here, not from a per-brand handle (a single LinkedIn company page typically represents the parent org, not each product). If you don't have a company page or post only to your personal feed, leave linkedin_company_id null.
org.name: Example Org

main._comment: Each brand under your org. The slug ('main', 'project_a', 'side_app') is what skills accept as their first arg. Add more sibling keys for additional brands.

instagram._comment: default_account is the label passed to /instagram-post and used as the .env credential prefix (INSTAGRAM_<UPPERCASE_LABEL>_USERNAME). own_handle is YOUR account handle as it appears on IG (no @) — used by /instagram-warm to skip your own posts in the feed AND by /instagram-post's post-publish verification step to build the correct profile URL. Set own_handle ONLY when it differs from default_account (e.g. label 'swiftbible' but actual IG handle '@swift_bible' with underscore). When unset or equal, default_account is used as the URL slug.

x._comment: default_handle is what /x-warm targets and what composite skills pass to /x-post when you invoke them under this brand. own_handle skips your own tweets in the warm feed. topic_filter_regex is the case-insensitive regex /x-warm matches against tweet text — likes only fire on tweets that match. exclude_handles_substring is a comma-separated list of substrings; any author handle containing one is skipped (use for parody / impersonation risk).

pinterest._comment: default_account is your Pinterest username (no @, no slash). default_board is where /post-daily-content publishes. feature_board is where /feature-post publishes (Pinterest's algorithm splits 'evergreen' from 'how-to / explainer' — keep them on different boards). topic_filter_regex gates which pins /pinterest-warm will save.

brand._comment: Surface-level metadata used in caption templates. name is what skills call the brand in caption boilerplate. url is the destination link auto-included in posts. voice is a freeform 1-2 sentence description /feature-post and /post-daily-content can use to tone the caption draft.
brand.name: My Brand

_example_second_brand._comment: Delete this stub if you only have one brand. It's here to show what a multi-brand setup looks like — e.g. an org named 'Acme Inc' with two products 'gizmo' and 'widget'. Each gets its own handles and topic filter; both post to the SAME LinkedIn company page (org.linkedin_company_id) under the parent org.
